description:
FILED s535a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08), found by accident while probing (scratch/s535a/pr/px3.pl).  A PPI tokenizer bug, the §19 family (docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §19 / §19b: a sub named `x` lexed as the repetition operator) -- this is a NEW variant: the sub's name is `x` FOLLOWED BY DIGITS.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    sub x3 { print "called\n" }
    x3();
    sub y3 { print "y called\n" }
    y3();

perl:              called / y called
main 06a4b8ba:     y called      -- SILENT WRONG: the x3() call is gone

PPI (vendored, pcl branch) for `sub x3 { 1 }\nx3();`:
    Word sub, Word x3, { Number 1 }, Operator x  <-- WRONG, Number 3  <-- WRONG, ( ) ;
expected: Word x3, Structure ( ), Structure ;   (a statement cannot start with the infix `x`).

PCL then lowers `x3();` as `(p-str-x (progn) 3)` -- the empty list repeated 3 times; nothing announced.  `Pl::Parser2::_repair_word_x_call` (§19b's repair) does not reach it: it looks for a Word/Operator `x` that is the first child of its statement followed by a call, and here PPI also split the NUMBER off the name.

Which names: any `x<digits>` sub (x1, x2, x64 ...) called right after a sub definition's closing brace (the §19b position).  Belongs to the PPI batch (fix on the `pcl` branch in PPI's two-commit shape, a registry row in Pl/PPIBugs.pm, a docs/ppi-bug-report.t row).

=== DONE (s536j) ===
FIXED on PCL's PPI branch: group AW, commit e45f69ab (tests 845b663c) on branch pcl -- PPI::Tokenizer::_current_x_is_operator asks _after_statement_block (the rule the `-` / `/` / `<` decisions already use): after the } of a block that ends a statement or takes a list perl does not expect an operator (toke.c: case 'x' tests PL_expect == XOPERATOR), so `x3`, `x64`, `x` are words there.  _after_statement_block learns a sub body after a prototype or attributes (_before_sub_decorations) and a block after the ) of a compound statement's condition, a foreach list or a named sub's signature (_paren_heads_statement_block), so `if (1) { } -e $f` is a filetest too.  Controls kept: `$a x3`, `do { } x3`, `{ a => 1 } x 2`, `sub ($) { } x 2`, `(1,2) x3`, `$h{a} x3`, `do { 5 } -1`.  Catalogue §63, registry row 63, report rows 383-400.
The same rule fixes §19b (`sub x { } x`, report row 29 out of TODO): the statement-start arm of Pl::Parser2::_repair_word_x_call + _starts_statement DELETED (ea8b244c) after an instrument-die run never fired (469e2961; wide A/B 2,053 files SAME 2052 / DIFF 1 = Math/Complex.pm (#4701) / RCDIFF 0).  §19's own arm (`print x()`) stays.
Probes perl -> main -> tree (scratch/s536j/p/x1.pl, 17 shapes): tree = perl; main dropped x3() after map / if / BEGIN / decorated subs.  Guard Pl/t/ppi-token-rows-01.t r29 (FAIL on 3139fcb0).
subject: SILENT WRONG (PPI): a sub named x<N> (x3, x64 ...) called right after a sub definition (`sub x3 {...} x3();`) is lexed as the repetition operator `x` + a number -- the call is dropped (the §19b family, a new variant)
